summary:
All four ratings are locked in on trends right now — 62% at n=152 over the last 14 days, a full 5.7 points above season baseline across R1, R2, R3 and R4 alike — and that category is the single biggest lever on today's board. Strong-play units confirm the heat is real, not noise: R4 is +24.0u over its last 7 days (74%, n=34) and R3 is riding +91.0u for the season at 57%, the best full-year strong-play mark in the shop. R3's runs category is also scorching at 60% (91-61, n=152, +6.8pts hot) despite sitting on a 3-game "cold streak" tag — worth noting the model still likes it that much even while grinding through a rough patch.

Today's slate hands full four-way consensus to 13 of 15 games, and the strongest one lines up perfectly with the hot trends signal: DET over WSN at +2.70 to +2.85 across all four ratings is the largest average delta on the board, and with trends+sp combining for 57.8% (350-256) as the top category pairing, a DET pick backed by both trend and starting-pitcher signal (Kent vs Anderson) is as clean as it gets today. ARI @ COL is the other extreme — full consensus fading ARI at -2.26 to -2.59, essentially a mirror image of the DET setup. BAL over TOR is another lean-in spot: BAL sits at 52% straight-up when picked this season but has actually cashed at 42% strong-play (-3.0u), so trust the trends signal here more than the team tag. LAD's the standout team-support play — 70% overall, 82% strong (27-6, +27.0u) — and today's LAD-over-SDP lean, while modest in delta (+0.74 to +1.85), rides one of the model's best team profiles. The two split games, HOU/SEA and LAA/ATH, are the only spots where the ratings disagree — both feature deltas under half a run, so treat them as pass-or-small plays rather than forcing a side.
